{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABXS2a8w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhA2qRo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 109, "title": "Simplify Graph Editor and Live UI with canvas-first and output-first layouts", "body": "## Problem

The Chrome Extension's **Graph Editor** and **Live** windows are visually crowded with long permanent explanations, redundant controls, verbose status text, and too much chrome around the actual graph/transcription. The current UI asks users to read instructions that should instead be communicated by layout, grouping, labels, affordances, and progressive disclosure.

This is a **UI/UX simplification and layout** task, not a change to the graph processing semantics. Use the previously researched products as **interaction/layout references**, not as code dependencies or exact visual copies:
- [React Flow workflow editor](https://reactflow.dev/ui/templates/workflow-editor): canvas-first layout, contextual node/wire controls, compact viewport actions.
- [Node-RED editor](https://nodered.org/docs/user-guide/editor/): palette/search, node selection, settings/help separation.
- [ComfyUI](https://docs.comfy.org/): easy port recognition, fast node discovery.
- [Otter.ai](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/360049722894-Otter-Quick-Start-Guide): output-first live transcript and compact recording controls.
- [Granola](https://www.granola.ai/): reduce always-visible UI to the current task.

## Expected outcome

### Graph Editor: make the graph the focus

- Remove the long always-visible prose above the editor in `extension/graph-editor.html` and the long `this.hint` instruction paragraph in `extension/graph-editor.js`. Do **not** replace them with another permanently visible tutorial. Keep detailed usage instructions accessible via a compact Help affordance or existing docs when requested.
- Give the **graph canvas most of the available space** on desktop, with clear node/port/wire affordances and accessible, discoverable zoom/fit controls.
- Consolidate the crowded toolbar into a clear primary action (Save), concise saved/unsaved/active-session indicators, and secondary commands (e.g. reset, load, validate) through a compact and discoverable UI. Do not silently apply or discard changes. Existing draft/save semantics and warnings on external changes must remain intelligible and actionable.
- Make adding Nodes straightforward through a **searchable, categorized palette** (source/input, processors, constants/utilities, outputs as appropriate). Avoid a permanently expanded giant button list. No need to adopt React Flow or another graph library.
- Show the settings inspector **contextually when a Node is selected**; provide useful editable settings immediately and move long `definition.help` prose/contract explanations to optional help/details. When nothing is selected, don't occupy a large column merely to display instructions.
- Keep wire selection/disconnection, drag/click connection, occupied-input replacement, keyboard operations, zoom and touch controls. Do not regress the existing on-canvas Disconnect affordance.
- Remove or consolidate the permanently visible draft translation fieldset and the obsolete fixed TranslateGemma footer in ways that reflect the actual graph/model state. Translation and language are graph/model-specific; avoid misleading global affordances. Do not remove any supported translation capability or necessary configuration.

### Live: make the transcript/output the focus

- Give **configured LiveTextDisplay outputs** visual priority over the capture/status controls. Support zero, one, or multiple graph-driven display regions without introducing a hardcoded single Transcript/Translation view.
- Use compact, clear Start/Stop/Cancel and recording-state presentation; retain current capture target, essential progress/errors, model recovery and audio output functionality, but visually consolidate low-priority status rows and reveal optional target controls only when needed.
- Make **committed text** vs **provisional preview** visually distinguishable without requiring explanatory paragraphs. Preserve exact `replace`/`append` behavior, copy, accumulated final text, and stable incremental rendering; use plain text safely.
- Keep accessibility: visible focus, semantic labels, screen-reader status/error announcements, contrast, keyboard navigation, touch targets, reduced-motion handling, and usable narrow-window layouts. Do not make critical controls icon-only without accessible names/tooltips.

### Scope and implementation

- Reuse the existing extension's HTML/CSS/JS and graph runtime. **No unrelated redesign, new UI framework, graph library migration, backend rewrite, or Node/Port behavior changes.**
- Consider hierarchy, spacing, typography, color and responsive layouts consistently across Graph Editor and Live. Avoid copying third-party branding or assets.
- Retain details in concise accessible Help or documentation rather than reintroducing permanent paragraphs. Only actionable errors and meaningful statuses should take persistent visual space when relevant.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Long permanent Graph Editor introductory paragraph and JS instruction/hint paragraph are gone from the default view; detailed help remains accessible on demand.
- [ ] A user can discover and add Nodes through search/categories, connect/disconnect edges, edit a selected Node, zoom/fit, save, reset/load and validate without relying on visible tutorial prose. Automated UI tests cover primary routes.
- [ ] The editor prioritizes canvas space, inspector appears contextually, and active/unsaved/saved/external-change states and validation errors remain clear and correct.
- [ ] Translation/model affordances are truthful for the actual graph; current translation routes/settings remain available without a permanent unrelated translation settings block or obsolete notice.
- [ ] Live output regions are visually primary; provisional vs committed text are clearly distinct; recording/capture/model statuses, errors, controls, optional target settings, copy, generated audio and multiple/no Live display modes remain functional.
- [ ] Keyboard and touch affordances, focus management, accessible names/status announcements and responsive narrow-window behavior are checked by deterministic browser and packaged MV3 tests where feasible.
- [ ] Refresh relevant screenshots and documentation to reflect the new layouts. Run applicable unit, browser and packaged extension suites plus `npm run build:extension` before merge; report actual results/skips accurately.
- [ ] No change to graph schema, ASR model behavior, translation semantics, capture lifecycle, persistent graph behavior or pipeline contracts except what is strictly required to preserve UI actions.

All mandatory checks must be achievable **before merge**, with no after-deployment acceptance blocker.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Context

- `extension/graph-editor.html`: long introductory prose and global `translation-settings` fieldset, plus old footer.
- `extension/graph-editor.js`: large permanent `this.hint` string, many toolbar buttons, full list of palette buttons, inspector that renders extensive help and port descriptions even for routine editing.
- `extension/recorder.html`: capture/status/control panel precedes `#live-displays`; several persistent informational rows.
- `extension/recorder.css`: current fixed three-column workspace, compact-window breakpoints and Live presentation.
- Previous #105 removed the instructional footer in Live; **do not bring it back**. This Issue tackles the wider interaction and layout problem.
- Prior research identified React Flow + Node-RED interaction patterns for Graph Editor and Otter.ai output-first visual hierarchy for Live as the closest reference direction.
